_meta.description: Curated list of fraud indicators specific to Canadian immigration scams targeting Spanish-speaking immigrants. Update weekly. Sources: Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre (CAFC), IRCC public alerts, College of Immigration & Citizenship Consultants (CICC) disciplinary records, and user-reported cases.

legitimate_ircc_email_subjects_format: Reference application or UCI numbers in standard format
fraudulent_domain_red_flag_patterns: Domains containing 'ircc' but NOT ending in .gc.ca
Domains containing 'canada' but NOT ending in canada.ca or .gc.ca
Top-level domains other than .ca or .gc.ca claiming Canadian government
Newly registered domains (less than 2 years old) claiming to be IRCC
Subdomains of free hosting (.netlify.app, .vercel.app, .github.io) claiming to be official
fraudulent_payment_methods: Gift cards (iTunes, Google Play, Amazon, Steam)
Wire transfer to a personal individual (not Receiver General for Canada)
Interac e-Transfer to a personal email (real IRCC fees go through canada.ca portal only)
PayPal to a personal account claiming to be 'IRCC officer'
Direct bank deposit to a personal account number
legitimate_payment_method: All real IRCC fees are paid online through the canada.ca portal only. Recipient is 'Receiver General for Canada'. Never to a person. Never via crypto, wire, gift card, Western Union, or e-Transfer to an individual.
urgency_red_flag_phrases_en: your visa will be cancelled today
guaranteed_approval_red_flags_es: puedo agilizar su caso por dentro
guaranteed_approval_red_flags_en: I have a contact at IRCC
I can speed up your case internally
personal_info_never_requested_by_email_o: Full passport scan via WhatsApp/email (real IRCC asks via secure portal)
ircc_does_not_use_for_official_communica: SMS / text messages (except basic notifications, never asking for payment or info)
Free email providers (Gmail, Yahoo, Hotmail, Outlook.com, Proton)
Zoom / Skype calls demanding immediate payment

spanish_speaker_targeted_scams.name: El falso notario WhatsApp
spanish_speaker_targeted_scams.description_es: Una persona se hace pasar por 'notario' canadiense y ofrece tramitar visa de inmigración por WhatsApp. Pide pagos por Western Union o transferencia bancaria personal. En Canadá los notarios NO tramitan inmigración — solo abogados o RCIC autorizados.
indicators: Pide pago por Western Union/transferencia personal

spanish_speaker_targeted_scams.name: Oferta de trabajo falsa con LMIA
spanish_speaker_targeted_scams.description_es: Le ofrecen un trabajo en Canadá con LMIA aprobado pero piden $5,000-$15,000 USD por adelantado para 'procesar el LMIA'. Los empleadores reales NUNCA cobran al trabajador por un LMIA — eso es ilegal.
indicators: Empresa con sitio web nuevo o inexistente

spanish_speaker_targeted_scams.name: Caso de patrocinio express
spanish_speaker_targeted_scams.description_es: Alguien promete patrocinio matrimonial garantizado por $20,000-$30,000. Real fee de patrocinio es ~$1,135 CAD. No existen 'patrocinios garantizados'.
indicators: Costos muy superiores a fees oficiales

spanish_speaker_targeted_scams.name: El refund/reembolso falso de CRA
spanish_speaker_targeted_scams.description_es: Un mensaje SMS dice que tiene un reembolso pendiente de Canada Revenue Agency relacionado con su trámite migratorio y que haga clic en un enlace. CRA NO comunica reembolsos por SMS.

spanish_speaker_targeted_scams.name: Estudio en Canadá con admisión garantizada
spanish_speaker_targeted_scams.description_es: Una 'agencia educativa' garantiza admisión a una universidad canadiense + visa de estudiante por un pago grande. Las admisiones reales las da la universidad directamente, no agentes.
indicators: Universidades de baja reputación o falsas

format_red_flags_visual: Logo IRCC borroso o de baja resolución
Tipografía inconsistente (varias fuentes en mismo documento)
Errores ortográficos en términos oficiales (IRCCC, Inmigration Canada, Citisenship)
Maple leaf incorrecto o de proporciones extrañas
Pie de página con dirección postal inexistente o que no coincide con dirección oficial IRCC
Encabezado dice 'IRCC' pero contenido habla en términos genéricos sin números de caso reales
real_ircc_communication_patterns: References specific UCI (Unique Client Identifier) number — 8-10 digits in format 1234-5678 or 1234-5678-90
References application number in proper IRCC format
Does NOT request payment via email — directs to canada.ca portal
Does NOT threaten deportation, arrest, or imminent visa cancellation
Provides official phone number 1-888-242-2100 for verification
Letter has IRCC letterhead with high-resolution maple leaf and proper Government of Canada wordmark
high_severity_indicators: Domain age less than 2 years claiming IRCC
Domain not in legitimate_ircc_domains but mentions IRCC/Canada immigration
Personal cell phone or WhatsApp claiming to be IRCC
Threatens deportation in less than 7 days
medium_severity_indicators: Free email provider (gmail/yahoo) claiming IRCC role
Spelling/grammar errors in supposedly official document
Logo or seal appears low resolution or distorted
References 'agent' or 'officer' by first name only
Communication only in one language when bilingual is standard
low_severity_indicators: Generic greeting (Dear Applicant) instead of name
Email signature missing official department line
